messages:
incident-bot: [P1] Solaris-Health (dedicated AZ pool) - elevated tail latency and queued requests > 95th pct for last 6m. Page routed to oncall team. link: https://incidents.redwood/s/3955551234 :warning:

maya (oncall): saw it, joining. swapping to thread for Solaris-Health dedicated queue.

jorge: placing initial hypothesis — tenant is spiking long responses, causing max_batch_tokens to inflate queuing. noticed many requests with long prompt prefixes.

devon: can we drop max_batch_tokens for that tenant temporarily? what knob controls that currently in scheduler v2?

maya (oncall): it's `tenant_scheduler.max_batch_tokens` per-tenant override. default 2048, Solaris override is 4096. lowering should reduce queue wait but may increase GPU utilization.

samir: FYI Solaris is on Azure West EU, dedicated pool nodes are 8xA10Gq. we've got spare capacity in other AZs but policy forbids cross-region fallback for this tenant.

maya (oncall): ok plan: 1) lower max_batch_tokens to 1024 for Solaris tenant 2) tighten scheduler burst_window to 200ms 3) enable aggressive KV prefix caching for commonly seen prompt signatures 4) observe tail latency 2m windows and rollback if errors spike.

ryan: +1. who will make the change?

jorge: I can push the change. will do a canary on one node in the dedicated pool first. command below to patch override via infra API:

```
# canary patch for tenant override
curl -X PATCH "https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/tenants/solar-tenant/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scheduler": {"max_batch_tokens": 1024, "burst_window_ms": 200}}'
```

maya (oncall): make sure to target node `solar-dedicated-01` first and add `?dry_run=false` omitted if you want immediate. Also annotate the change with `incident:3955551234` so we can correlate.

jorge: starting canary now. tail logs: `tail -n 200 /var/log/serving/solar-dedicated-01/scheduler.log`

incident-bot: change requested by jorge: PATCH queued -> solar-dedicated-01 (canary). ETA apply 15s. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jorge: applied. canary reports: scheduler accepted override, active batch token cap 1.02k, seen immediate drop in queued count from 42 -> 9 on that node.

devon: checking p99 latency across pool: before canary p99 overall 1.1s, after canary p99 down to 820ms in that node. still saw some requeue churn.

samir: noticed GPU mem headroom reduced for canary node by ~6% due to smaller batches; throughput per GPU decreased ~8% but latency improvement is primary for customer SLAs.

maya (oncall): continue to roll to rest of nodes one-at-a-time with 30s pause and watch error rate. roll only if requeues do not spike >2% and cpu/gpu OOM metrics stable.

jorge: rolling now to solar-dedicated-{02,03,04} with 30s between. applying same PATCH, tagging incident id.

ryan: watch `serve_error_rate` and `requeue_count`. set alert if requeue_count > 50 in 1m for any node.

incident-bot: metric alert suppressed for this incident for 10m window to avoid distracting noise.

devon: after roll to all nodes p99 dropped cluster-wide from 1.1s -> 760ms, queued requests fell by 68%. error-rate unchanged at 0.12%.

maya (oncall): good. now enabling KV prefix caching for Solaris tenant to reduce repeated prefix tokenization cost. this is a safe toggle but requires warming.

jorge: enabling caching via controlplane toggle: `tenant_cache.prefix.enabled=true` -> applied. expect hit-rate ramp over 5-10m.

samir: cache hit-rate on solar nodes climbing: 12% -> 55% in 7m. throughput per node improved, and tail latency improved further to 640ms.

maya (oncall): final step: evaluate if we can keep lowered max_batch_tokens as permanent tenant override or instead create dynamic rule: if queue_depth > 30 then lower to 1024 else 2048. thoughts?

ryan: dynamic rule nicer but adds complexity to scheduler. could roll as feature flag behind `dynamic_tenant_batching`.

devon: short term, I'd prefer permanent override to 1536 (middle ground) for 24h and monitor. then follow with a scheduled change to introduce dynamic rule in next sprint.

maya (oncall): agreed. set temp override 1536 for 24h. Jorge, can you patch that and add an alert to re-evaluate in 24h?

jorge: patched override -> 1536 for Solaris with ttl 24h. added ticket INC-3955551234-REVIEW.

incident-bot: Change summary: lowered max_batch_tokens (4096->1536), burst_window 200ms, enabled prefix caching. Incident annotated.

maya (oncall): status update to customer success and account team: Solaris-Health saw latency reduction and queue relief. No user-facing errors observed. Sending short incident note. @samir please confirm any billing/throughput impacts we should flag.

samir: throughput dip ~5% - cost delta minimal for now. no immediate billing action.

maya (oncall): handoff: I'm staying on until 02:00 UTC to watch the TTL, then hand to next oncall @ryan. leaving runbook entries in the incident ticket.

ryan: acknowledged, will take over monitoring and begin post-incident triage.

devon: postmortem action items I will own: 1) add dynamic batching RFC 2) add safer canary flag to controlplane to auto-check `requeue_count` before full roll 3) include tenant prompt-length histogram in console.

jorge: ops items: document exact PATCH commands and make a small helper script for tenants to toggle overrides safely.

maya (oncall): final note: great coordination. tagging this thread to incident ticket and closing paging. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Paging closed by maya (oncall). Incident severity downgraded to P2 - monitoring.

maya (oncall): will update customer with summary in 30m.

ryan: copying into handoff note: observed metrics, commands used, and TTL applied. will escalate to eng if we see requeue spike above threshold overnight.

devon: adding to retro board. thanks all. :thumbsup:
